May 21–22, 2027 · Virtual

The Faith + Mental Health Virtual Summit

Join us online for the 2027 Faith + Mental Health Summit on Friday and Saturday, May 21–22. This year the summit is fully virtual, so attendees from around the world can take part in expert-led discussions, practical strategies, and sessions on faith and mental wellness without travel. Friday also includes the Faith + Mental Health Awards ceremony.

By attending, faith leaders, community members, and health and wellness providers gain the tools, strategies, and resources needed to transform lives in their families and communities. Registrants have access to speakers, exclusive giveaways, practical handouts, training sessions, and networking.

Why this summit

There is an urgent need for education, resources, and practical strategies around health and wellness in our communities, including the church. Every day, people struggle with anxiety, depression, poverty, social isolation, health issues, and addiction. Many still suffer in silence because of stigma, lack of understanding, and shame.

This event bridges the gap between faith and holistic health, offering professional solutions and resources to address mental health where people live and worship.

Day 1 · OnlineFri, May 21

Speaker sessions and the Faith + Mental Health Awards ceremony.

Day 2 · OnlineSat, May 22

A full day of sessions across the conference tracks. Join from anywhere in the world.

Call for Speakers

We are now accepting speaker proposals for the 2027 Faith + Mental Health Virtual Summit: a global gathering for faith and mental wellness, held entirely online so we can reach a global audience.

Speaking slots are limited. We receive many more proposals than we can accept and are looking for a diverse lineup of speakers and topics across all tracks. All 2027 sessions are virtual.

Notification of acceptance by February 15, 2027. Please do not email asking for updates.

Apply to Speak

Your submission should include

  • An overview of your proposed talk
  • The conference track that best fits your topic
  • A brief biography
  • Contact information (phone and email)
  • Links to past presentations (optional, encouraged)

Trouble with the form? Email your submission to faithandmentalhealth1@gmail.com. Incomplete submissions will not be considered. Keep a copy for your records.

Expectations

  • This is a mental health education conference, not a motivational speaking platform.
  • Submissions centered only on sermons, revival-style messages, books, or personal testimonies without clinical or evidence-based grounding will not be considered.
  • We do not accept presentations that promote unverified healing claims, unfounded cures, or content that discourages professional mental health care.
  • All content should show ethical responsibility and respect for the complexity of mental health conditions.
  • Submissions must come directly from the presenter (no third-party submissions). Selected contributors are not paid an honorarium. Every presentation should be clinically sound.

Conference tracks

  • Family and Marriage
  • Addiction and Recovery
  • Counselor
  • Faith and Mental Health
  • Ethnic Minority
  • Neuroscience and Psychiatry
  • Child and Adolescent
  • Anxiety, Grief, and Depression
  • Holistic Health (Wellness + Nutrition)
  • Mental Health, General (treatment, research)

Topic examples

Examples only, not a guide. We are not looking for sermons, testimonials, or self-promotion.

Faith-based approaches to mental healthTrauma and healing in faith communitiesMental health advocacyYouth and mental wellnessIntegrative and holistic careCounseling, therapy, and pastoral careMaternal mental healthBreakthroughs in psychiatric careBrain healthArt and music for mental healthWorld mental healthSpiritually integrated Mental Health First AidHow clergy should address a mental health crisisStarting a mental health ministrySpiritual issues vs. mental health conditionsRecognizing the need for psychiatric careSupport strategies for caregiversAddressing chronic stressHoardingGrief, depression, and anxiety

Review and speaker coordination

Every proposal is reviewed for fit. When several submissions cover similar topics, we select the one that best fits the summit's goals. You will receive an email confirming we received your submission, and all submitters will hear their status by February 15, 2027.

Mandatory Zoom session: all selected speakers must attend one Zoom session (date TBA). Speakers who do not attend are removed from the lineup.

Letters of Intent for Papers

We are accepting letters of intent for manuscripts to be included in our digital publication for the 2027 Faith + Mental Health Virtual Summit.

Your letter of intent should briefly describe your proposed submission (max 550 words). Name all authors and include a brief biography and contact information (phone and email). Incomplete submissions will not be considered. One submission per person.

Those selected will be invited to submit a full manuscript of 1,000 to 4,000 words that follows the provided guidelines. All manuscripts are reviewed and final acceptance is not guaranteed.

Under the research category, we welcome current research of any kind, including applied research, experimental research, program evaluations, and literature reviews.

The call for posters closes February 15, 2027. Acceptance notifications go out by February 28, 2027. Final work and supplemental materials are due April 20, 2027. Send submissions to faithandmentalhealth1@gmail.com.

2027 Faith + Mental Health Awards

Celebrate the work being done to integrate faith and mental health by nominating an outstanding individual, team, or organization. These awards recognize significant contributions to mental health advocacy, education, and innovation at local, national, and global levels. Nominees can be clinicians, advocates, or organizations, and the same nominee can be entered in all four categories where it fits.

Ralph and Bernice Cunningham Community Mental Health Award

Honors those improving mental health in underserved communities, including returning citizens, low-income populations, ethnic minorities, and other marginalized groups, through initiatives that promote wellness, access to care, and community support.

Faith + Mental Health Pioneer Award

Recognizes advocates, researchers, and innovators leading the integration of faith and mental health, including those educating faith communities and advocating for holistic approaches to well-being.

Global Mental Health Award

Celebrates work with global impact: delivering mental health solutions, resources, or advocacy to diverse populations worldwide, including training clinicians and support roles in other nations, in person or remotely.

Youth Mental Health Advocacy Award

Recognizes those raising awareness for youth mental health, including youth suicide prevention, substance abuse awareness, and other issues affecting young people's well-being.

Submit a Nomination

Nominate for the 2027 Awards

Eligibility: nominees must have made a significant contribution to their field within the past two years. Deadline: April 1, 2027.

Complete the nomination form with the nominee's name and contact, the award category, and a detailed description of their achievements and why they deserve the award. Winners will be announced and celebrated online on Friday, May 21, 2027 during the summit.

Mental Health in the Church · Training Institute

Equip. Empower. Transform culture.

The Faith + Mental Health Training Institute offers customized training that helps ministries, churches, and organizations build a mentally healthy, spiritually strong, and emotionally safe environment for leaders and the people they serve.

In person or virtual, we work with your leadership and team to build an integrated understanding of mental wellness that reflects your faith values, strengthens your internal culture, and supports long-term organizational health.

Who it's for

  • Church and ministry leadership teams
  • Nonprofit and faith-based organizations
  • Program staff, volunteers, and support workers
  • Community groups deepening wellness and support practices

Flexible format

  • In-person sessions
  • Virtual workshops
  • One-time intensives or ongoing training tracks

Mental Health & Wellness Integration

Make mental health part of your ministry or organizational mission, connecting faith-based principles with evidence-informed wellness practices without compromising either.

Creating a Supportive Culture

Build a culture that supports emotional well-being, encourages openness, and fosters creative problem-solving. A supportive environment is healthier, more productive, and more sustainable.

Destigmatizing Mental Health

Explore the roots of stigma in faith-based and cultural contexts and get tools to change those narratives. Your team will learn to talk about mental health with clarity, compassion, and confidence.

Behavior, Culture, and Mental Health

Examine how mental health concerns show up in organizational culture, through burnout, disconnection, or poor communication, and how to address them early and effectively.

We will assess your team's needs and build a training plan that fits your goals, schedule, and context. Creating a mentally healthy environment is essential: equip your team to serve others without neglecting their own well-being.

Book a Consultation
DSM-5 AND THE CHURCH Equipping the Church: A DSM-5 Guide to Mental Health, Diagnosis, and Response
Mental health and the church · 90-minute webinar

DSM-5 and the Church

Ministry leaders, can you recognize a mental health crisis in your congregation? Many believers are silently battling emotional and psychological distress. It's time for the church to become more equipped, informed, and compassionate.

This webinar helps faith leaders respond wisely to mental health challenges using insights from the DSM-5, the standard diagnostic tool used in clinical settings.

In this training, you'll learn

  • How to recognize key signs and symptoms of mental health disorders
  • Who can diagnose, and how diagnoses are made using the DSM-5
  • When and how to refer people for professional help
  • How churches can offer spiritual support without overstepping clinical boundaries

All participants receive online access to the DSM-5 and the Church e-book.

For pastors, ministry leaders, care team members, and church counselors. New dates will be announced; churches can also request a private session for their team.

Meet the founder

D'Andrea Bolden

D'Andrea Bolden, the visionary founder of Faith + Mental Health, is a prolific writer who enjoys writing nonfiction books for a diverse audience. She is a gifted communicator and a sought-after speaker for mental health, corporate, and faith-based events.

D'Andrea has earned a Bachelor's Degree in Psychology with a minor in Chemistry, a Master's Degree in Counseling, and a Master's Degree in Medical Sciences. In addition to her academic achievements, she has also earned a certification in AI Development.

Her extensive work in the nonprofit sector reflects her commitment to community impact. She has developed innovative programs and camps that promote STEM education, youth entrepreneurship, and family support services. As host of the annual Faith + Mental Health Summit and the Faith + Mental Health Podcast, she advocates for the integration of faith and science in holistic health practices.

She is passionate about the intersection of faith and health, understanding that scientific evidence supports the benefits of an integrative, multidimensional, holistic approach. Ultimately, D'Andrea wants to see the faith-based community free of stigma and knowledgeable about how to address every aspect of health.

As an author, she has published several books, including Black Health: Considered From A Holistic Perspective. D'Andrea lives in Michigan with her husband, John, and their two children.

Who we are

Our Mission

Faith + Mental Health exists to bridge the gap between faith and mental health through training, partnerships, events, writing, and video.

Mission

Why we exist

To bridge the gap between faith and mental health by providing quality trainings, community and professional partnerships, educational events, writings, and videos. We are strong believers in holistic health and will continue to advocate for integrative, holistic mental health care for everyone.

Vision

Where we're going

A safe space where faith and mental health operate together for the good of people in need of traditional or integrative professional services, all the way down to the community level. We will keep working to end the stigma and misconceptions that disproportionately cause minorities and the faith-based community to avoid professional mental health services.

Resource Provision

Maintain and expand a directory of providers, e-learning opportunities, and events that equip faith communities and individuals with tools for mental health support.

Education and Awareness

Develop and share educational materials, including articles, blog posts, and courses, that deepen understanding of where faith and mental health meet.

Community Engagement

Host events like the annual Faith + Mental Health Summit to connect faith leaders, mental health professionals, and community members.

Advocacy

Promote the integration of faith and mental health in public discourse, reduce stigma, and encourage holistic approaches to well-being.

Steering Committee

Guided by experts and leaders

The Faith + Mental Health Steering Committee guides and supports the mission of bridging the gap between faith and mental health. Drawing on its members' expertise, the committee provides strategic direction, ensures accountability, and fosters collaboration among faith leaders, mental health professionals, and the community.

Through its work, the committee aims to create environments where spiritual and mental health care work together to support individuals and communities in need.

The committee is dedicated to

  • Promoting awareness and education about the intersection of faith and mental health
  • Advocating to reduce stigma and misconceptions about mental health in faith-based and minority communities
  • Helping develop and carry out programs, events, and resources aligned with holistic well-being
  • Monitoring progress and keeping the initiative aligned with its mission and objectives
Places to get help

Resources

If you or someone you know is in immediate danger, call 911 or go to the nearest emergency room.

988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline

Call or text 988

En español: press 2. Free, confidential, 24/7 crisis counseling and referrals through a national network of local crisis centers. The former number, 1-800-273-8255, still connects.

Chat online

Crisis Text Line

Text HOME to 741741

Available 24/7 across the U.S. for anyone in any type of crisis, connecting you with a trained crisis counselor.

crisistextline.org

Veterans Crisis Line

Dial 988, press 1

Or text 838255. Free, confidential, 24/7 support for all veterans, even those not registered with the VA.

Veterans Crisis Chat

Disaster Distress Helpline

1-800-985-5990

Call or text. Immediate, multilingual crisis counseling for emotional distress related to any natural or human-caused disaster, 24/7.

samhsa.gov

Worried about a friend's social media posts? Contact the platform directly, or dial 911 in an emergency.

General

National Alliance on Mental Illness (NAMI)
The largest nationwide grassroots mental health advocacy organization, with hundreds of state organizations, affiliates, and volunteers. A hub for support groups, free education, and community. NAMI HelpLine: 1-800-950-NAMI (6264).
Mental Health Resources (MHR)
A nonprofit providing community-based mental health services to adults, especially those with medical, social, or substance-related comorbidities.
American Psychiatric Association
The world's largest professional organization of psychiatrists, with patient education on a range of conditions plus news, research, and policy developments.

Government

MedlinePlus: Mental Health
The National Library of Medicine's collection on conditions, treatments, research, medications, terminology, and clinical trials.
World Health Organization: Mental Health Atlas
Global data on mental health policy, prevalence, services, medicines, and professionals, searchable by region or country.
U.S. Department of Health & Human Services: Mental Health
Government information drawn from the CDC, NIH, NIMH, MedlinePlus, and SAMHSA for the public, providers, policymakers, schools, and communities.

Ethnic / Minority Mental Health

Therapy for Black Girls
Therapist locator, community, and articles supporting the wellness of Black women and girls.
Black Mental Health Alliance
Connects individuals with therapists and provides professional training.
BEAM: Black Emotional and Mental Health Collective
Mental health training, toolkits, and a directory of licensed Black therapists offering online services.
Asian American Psychological Association
Fact sheets on trauma, violence exposure, intimate partner violence, student adjustment, bullying, and suicide.
Asians Do Therapy
Reduces stigma and improves access to therapy, with guidance on finding a therapist.
Asian Mental Health Collective
Raises awareness in Asian diasporic communities and maintains a nationwide APIDA therapist directory.
Latinx Therapy
A directory of therapists and helpful information for the Latinx community.
Therapy for Latinx
Verified therapists, psychiatrists, clinics, emergency mental health, and support groups for the Latinx community.
National Alliance for Hispanic Health
Health information plus a helpline (866-783-2645) for help navigating the health system.
Tribal Affairs, SAMHSA
Government services for Native American communities. SAMHSA National Helpline: 1-800-662-4357.
Behavioral Health, Indian Health Service
Information on behavioral health, mental health, and suicide prevention.
Center for Native American Youth
Tools including videos, peer-to-peer engagement activities, and a resource exchange.

Substance Use

Smokefree.gov
Created by the CDC and NIH, with ideas and downloadable resources for quitting tobacco plus online and phone counseling contacts.
SAMHSA
Information on all kinds of substance use disorders for the public, families, health professionals, and schools.
FindTreatment.gov
SAMHSA's treatment finder for locating a substance use treatment provider near you.

Eating Disorders

ANAD
Information on eating disorders, how to seek treatment, and free support groups for people with eating disorders and their families.
National Alliance for Eating Disorders
Free therapist-led support groups, a treatment referral helpline (1-866-662-1235), and resources for families and school professionals.

Training

Mental Health First Aid
Courses that teach you to recognize and respond to signs of mental health and substance use challenges.
